articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Sanctions Targeting Narcotics Trafficking and Terrorism Financing Networks
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These actions aim to disrupt financial networks that support illicit drug trade and terrorist organizations globally, underscoring the U.S. commitment to combating these threats.
The specific individuals and entities designated were not immediately detailed in the initial announcement but are expected to be added to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Sanctions List, Reinforcing Pressure on Tehran
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an Iran Designation Update on November 9, 2026, modifying existing sanctions against entities and individuals connected to the Iranian regime.
This action is part of ongoing efforts to exert economic pressure on Iran, particularly concerning its nuclear program and support for regional destabilizing activities.
The update includes additions and modifications to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, further restricting Iran's access to the international financial system.

articles.headline: U.S. Imposes New Iran-Related Sanctions Targeting Financial Networks
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026, aimed at crippling financial networks that sustain the Iranian regime.
These sanctions are part of a broader strategy to disrupt the financing of Iran's proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities and ballistic missile program, as well as its malign regional activities.
The action targets individuals and entities providing financial support to the Iranian government, further isolating Tehran from the global financial system.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / U.S. Department of State

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber and Transnational Criminal Organizations; Expands Cuba Sanctions to Key Economic Sectors
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 5, 2026, targeting cyber-related threats and transnational criminal organizations.

Concurrently, OFAC expanded its Cuba sanctions program by issuing a determination that extends Executive Order 14404 to four additional sectors of the Cuban economy: manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine.

This move aims to further restrict the Cuban regime's access to revenue and resources, with the State Department also designating eight entities and two individuals, and identifying five vessels as blocked property, for supporting Cuba's oil shipping networks, state-owned entities, and military supply chains.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / U.S. Department of State

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Sanctions, Issues Alert on Shadow Fleet, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 4, 2026, alongside updates to certain Iran-related listings.

In a significant move, OFAC also published an Iran-related alert, warning of the sanctions risks associated with dealing with potentially false-flagged vessels used by Iran's 'shadow fleet' for sanctions evasion.

Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question, providing updated guidance on transactions involving the Petroleos de Venezuela, S.A. (PDVSA) 2020 8.5% bond.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.
This amendment modifies existing authorizations for certain transactions involving Iran, reflecting ongoing adjustments to the U.S. sanctions policy.
The specifics of the amendments were not immediately detailed but typically relate to humanitarian trade, personal remittances, or other permitted activities under the Iran sanctions program.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities in North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities in North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).
These actions aim to counter threats posed by North Korea's weapons of mass destruction programs and address human rights abuses and corruption in the DRC.
The designations underscore the U.S. commitment to using sanctions to promote international security and human rights.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026, regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These updates provide clarification and guidance to financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations under OFAC regulations.
The amendments aim to enhance understanding and adherence to sanctions requirements, particularly concerning the proper handling and reporting of blocked or rejected transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Removes Belarus and North Korea Entities, and Issues New GLs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026, while also removing certain entities from the sanctions lists related to Belarus and North Korea.
In a multifaceted action, OFAC also issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses, alongside amended Frequently Asked Questions, providing updated guidance on authorized transactions.
These actions reflect a dynamic approach to sanctions policy, adjusting measures based on geopolitical developments and specific compliance considerations.

articles.headline: UK Adds 20 Entities to Russia Sanctions List, Targets Oil Tanker 'APEKS'
body: On November 12, 2026, the UK's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office updated the UK Sanctions List, adding 20 new entities and implementing one variation under The Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019.
Among the new designations is the oil tanker 'APEKS' (IMO 9274616), owned by Global Seaway LLC and believed to be flagged in Russia.

The UK government stated that there are reasonable grounds to suspect 'APEKS' has been involved in activities destabilizing Ukraine or undermining its territorial integrity, specifically by carrying Russian-origin oil or oil products to a third country.

articles.headline: 2026 Marked by Extreme Weather Events and Escalating Climate Crisis
body: The year 2026 has been characterized by unprecedented extreme weather events globally, including choking fires, deadly heatwaves, and devastating floods, with the death toll already in the high tens of thousands.

The World Meteorological Organization reports an alarming buildup of energy in Earth's system, with over 90% stored in oceans, leading to more extreme weather and threatening health and food supplies.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres has declared the global climate in a state of emergency, emphasizing that 'Planet Earth is being pushed beyond its limits' and 'every key climate indicator is flashing red.'

articles.headline: BIS Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors, Transfers to EAR
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced that, effective November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR), rather than the State Department's U.S. Munitions List.

This deregulatory action aims to align export controls on suppressors with those already applied to firearms, reducing the compliance burden on the firearms industry while maintaining national security.

Under this new rule, suppressors will be added to the Commerce Control List (CCL), requiring a license for certain exports, reexports, or in-country transfers, including releases of related software and technology to foreign persons.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
